Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Additional Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 Dated this 7th day of December, 2024 Petitioner in Prathibha M., D/o Late Muniraju M., Mvc 4696/2021: Aged about 16 years, R/at Kadajakkanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka - 562 106. (Policy No.455100/31/2022/962, valid from 23-09-2021 to 22-09-2022) Insurer of vehicle No.KA-59-1425 (Sri M. Ramesha, Advocate) 2. Sri Anjaneya Logistics Pvt. texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are as follows : At that time, the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-59-1425 drove the same in rash and negligent manner, without caring for human safety and dashed to the two-wheeler of the deceased. Due to said impact, the petitioner in M.V.C. No.4696/2021, who was pillion rider on 4 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 the above two wheeler, fell down on the road and sustained injuries all over her body. Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Anekal Government Hospital for first aid, thereafter she was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and Y.K. Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, she was working as flower vendor and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity. Likewise, the deceased in M.V.C. No.4697/2021 fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over her body and succumbed to said injuries before she was shifted to Anekal Government Hospital. Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as flower vendor and milking cows and was C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 3 earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. She was contributing her entire earnings to her family. Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood. The Anekal Police have 5 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 registered the case against the driver of the said Eicher Canter for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petitions and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- in M.V.C. No.4696/2021 and Rs.30,00,000/- in M.V.C. No.4697/2021 with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petitions. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the 6 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 4 Eicher Canter bearing Reg. No.KA-59-1425 in favour of respondent No.2 and its validity as on the date of accident. It has contended that, the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-59-1425 and deceased/rider of the TVS Heavy Duty Moped were not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident and thereby they have violated the terms and conditions of the policy. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. It has contended that, the accident has not occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Canter. It has further contended that, the deceased and the pillion rider were not wearing helmet and the insured was running the vehicle without having valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of accident. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner and the deceased. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 7 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petitions. 5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the C. In order to prove their case, the natural guardian of the petitioner in M.V.C. No.4696/2021 and the petitioner No.1 in M.V.C. No.4697/2021 have got examined themselves as P.W.1 and P.W.2 respectively and got marked total 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20. The petitioner in M.V.C. No.4696/2021 has got examined one more witness namely Dr. K. M. Kumaraswamy as P.W.3. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined the driver of the offending 9 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 vehicle as R.W.1. But, after recording his examination-in- chief, as R.W.1 did not turned back to the Court for cross- examination, his evidence on record stands discarded. Further, the respondent No.1 has examined its authorised person/Assistant Manager as R.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2. 7. As per the final order, for the following: C. Issue No.1 in both the cases: It is specific case of the petitioners in M.V.C. Nos.4696/2021 and 10 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 M.V.C.No.4697/2021 that, on 16-10-2021 at about 2.15 p.m., near Muneshwar Temple, Kadujakkanahalli Indlawadi Cross road, Kasaba Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, when the petitioner in M.V.C. No.4696/2021 and deceased Sneha U., in M.V.C. No.4697/2021 were traveling on a two-wheeler bearing No.KA-51-R-7736 as pillion rider and rider respectively, slowly and cautiously, at that time the driver of offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-59-1425 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the two-wheeler of the deceased. Due to said impact, the rider and pillion rider fell down on the road and sustained injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner in M.V.C. No.4696/2021 was shifted to Anekal Government Hospital for first aid, thereafter she was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and Y.K. Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient. Whereas, the rider of said two- wheeler succumbed to injuries before she was shifted to Anekal Government Hospital. 11 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 10. In order to prove their case, the natural guardian of C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 8 petitioner in M.V.C. No.4696/2021 and petitioner No.1 in M.V.C. No.4697/2021 have got examined themselves as P.W.1 and P.W.2 respectively, by filing their examination-in- chief affidavit, wherein they have reiterated the entire averments made in the petition. In support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20.
texts.arguments: Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Saraswati Palariya V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., reported in LAW(SC) 2018 (8) 172, has clearly held that, "just because the deceased was driving the vehicle 15 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 11 without driving licence, it may expose the claimants to other liability, but no inference of contributory negligence cane be arrived on that basis." 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Mohammed Siddique and another V/s National Insurance Company Ltd., reported in AIR 2020 SC 520, has clearly held that, "the deceased was riding the motorcycle along with his friend, driver and guilt of violation of law cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that the very act of riding with two others contributed to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim." Due to said impact the rider and pillion rider C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 12 sustained severe injuries and the rider succumbed to said injuries before she was shifted tot he hospital. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the 21 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 18 he found that, the petitioner has suffered 1) diffuse edema involving lower 1/3rd of the face, 2) tenderness over the chin right ankle region, 3) tenderness over both knee joint, 4) sutured soft tissue seen in inner side of lower jaw and 5) nasal bleeding in the road traffic accident. Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 5% disability with respect to disocclusion of posterior teeth, 5% disability with respect to mobility of anterior teeth and 5% disability with respect to sensitivity of the teeth. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, " The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1). The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of . This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative. defined in the Act. As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 25 the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only. Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person. It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased. All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative". As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor 34 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child. In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation. In the concurring judgment of Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation". The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased. Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 26 application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only." But, as the deceased was a minor aged about 15 years as on the date of accident, as per the latest judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in M.F.A. No.11440/2011 C/W M.F.A. No.206/2018, dated 12-09-2024, Laxminarayanappa @ Moogappa and others v/s M/s Royal Sundaram Allianz Ins. Co. Ltd., Bengaluru and another, at page No.104, Table No.3.4 that, in case of death of a minor aged about 15 years or born in the year 2006, having both the parents, the compensation 38 MVC No.4696/2021 & 4697/2021 amount of Rs.6,76,754/- plus medical expenses if any is to be awarded towards pecunary loss to the dependents. Therefore, in the light of above cited decision and for the above stated reasons, as there are no medical bills produced by the petitioners, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners in the present case are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,76,754/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. In C. Umesh vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48740500/ 29 such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
